transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-27
Time: 15:32 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Leo Harris (Redwood SE), Julia Park (Arclight - Head of InfoSec), Marcus Lee (Arclight - Platform Lead), Anika Patel (Arclight - Legal)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery for potential Redwood deployment (evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Focus on SOC2/ISO attestation, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS flows, and data retention policies. Agreed to share artifacts and schedule in-depth infra + legal follow-up.

Topics:
- Compliance certifications (SOC2, ISO 27001)
- SSO/SAML integration and IdP metadata
- RBAC and least-privilege controls
- Audit logging, log retention and exportability
- Encryption at rest (KMS/HSM) and key ownership for Private/Dedicated
- Data residency and retention policies

Action items (recap):
- Redwood to send SOC2/ISO docs and security whitepaper
- SE to share architecture diagram for VPC/private deploy and KMS flow
- Customer to send compliance questionnaire and retention buckets
- Schedule follow-up with infra + legal

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're on for 55 minutes, I'll kick off. Uh, I'm Maya, AE here at Redwood, and Leo is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Julia Park: Hi Maya, Im Julia, Head of InfoSec at Arclight. Marcus and Anika are on with me. We're mainly looking to understand security differences between Hosted, Dedicated and Private options.
[00:22] Marcus Lee: Morning, and quick note — cost is a factor but security and data residency are priority.
[00:27] Leo Harris: Great, makes sense. I'll try to cover the technical implications on each deployment mode and where key controls live.
[00:34] Maya Chen: Quick agenda: certifications, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, retention and finally next steps. If we need a deep dive we'll sync infra + legal.
[00:44] Julia Park: Sounds good. First, certifications — do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001? Any recency on those?
[00:52] Maya Chen: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001. We'll send the attestations after this call. The latest SOC2 is from late 2025, ISO cert renewed 2025 as well. Ill attach the reports.
[01:05] Anika Patel: Are there limitations on redaction for the reports? Our legal wants to know what we can share internally.
[01:12] Maya Chen: Typically we provide full attestation under NDA; for prospective customers we can share redacted copies and then full copies under a mutual NDA. We'll include that note when we send.
[01:22] Julia Park: Okay good, that helps. Next, SSO — we run Okta and Azure AD. We need SAML support, SCIM for provisioning would be nice. What's the Redwood story?
[01:31] Leo Harris: We support SSO via SAML 2.0 and OIDC. SCIM provisioning is available for enterprise tiers and Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we do shared tenancy but SAML is supported via the control plane — you can map groups to RBAC roles.
[01:45] Marcus Lee: How are roles mapped? Can we enforce least-privilege and separate dev/prod access?
[01:50] Leo Harris: Yes, RBAC is role-based — admin, developer, auditor by default, and you can create custom roles. For Dedicated/Private you get more granular network-level controls too. Note: in some transcripts SAML gets transcribed as "Sam L" so apologies if the docs show odd casing.
[02:05] Julia Park: (laughs) Noted. On RBAC, does audit logging show which SSO user performed an action?
[02:12] Leo Harris: Audit logs capture user identifiers tied to SSO identity, timestamp, action, resource, IP. Logs are queryable in the Console and exportable via S3 or event webhooks for SIEM ingestion. For Dedicated/Private customers we can ship logs to your own SIEM.
[02:26] Anika Patel: Retention — we need 7 years for certain financial records. Is that possible? Also are logs immutable?
[02:33] Maya Chen: We support configurable retention windows. For Hosted we provide retention up to our max (we'll include actual retention buckets in the docs), and for Dedicated/Private customers you can configure long-term retention and even external archiving. Immutability is achieved through append-only storage with object versioning for audit trails; for regulatory needs we can work through contractual terms.
[02:52] Julia Park: Encryption at rest — do you use CMEK or only provider-managed keys? We prefer customer-managed keys.
[02:59] Leo Harris: For Hosted we use provider-managed keys by default but offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK)/CMEK for enterprise accounts. For Dedicated/Private, keys can be customer-controlled via KMS integrations or even HSMs if required — we'll document supported KMS providers and the key rotation policies.
[03:15] Marcus Lee: If we run Private on-prem, do we still have Redwood control plane? How does key ownership work then?
[03:22] Leo Harris: Private options can be shipped with a customer-managed control plane or a hybrid where metadata hooks back to Redwood. In full on-prem, you manage keys locally and we provide the deployment manifest; in VPC-hosted Private we support your KMS in your cloud account so keys never leave your tenancy. We'll send architecture diagrams.
[03:41] Julia Park: Good. Any certifications around HSM or FIPS for crypto?
[03:45] Maya Chen: We can share specifics; some of our partners use FIPS-compliant HSMs in Dedicated/Private setups. I'll include a note in the packet on FIPS/HSM support.
[03:56] Marcus Lee: What about data residency — we need EU-only processing for some workloads.
[04:01] Leo Harris: We support region pinning in Hosted for EU regions, Dedicated clusters can be spun up in specific regions, and Private obviously stays inside your network. For EU-only legal controls we can provide data flow diagrams and region isolation SLAs.
[04:15] Julia Park: Do you provide penetration test reports or DR test summaries?
[04:20] Maya Chen: We can provide summary results and remediation notes; full pentest reports may be redacted but available under NDA. DR/BC testing cadence is annual and we'll include high level outcomes.
[04:33] Anika Patel: On contractual terms - liability caps, breach notification timelines?
[04:38] Maya Chen: Standard enterprise contracts include incident notification within 72 hours and we negotiate liability clauses at enterprise tier — we'll have legal follow-up.
[04:46] Marcus Lee: Network-level controls — can Dedicated be provisioned with private subnets only and no public egress?
[04:53] Leo Harris: Yes, Dedicated supports private-only clusters with NAT or egress controls. You can also opt for no public IPs and peering into your VPC. For Hosted there are limitations but we provide transit options and proxy connectors.
[05:06] Julia Park: Any third-party audit integrations? SIEM connectors?
[05:10] Leo Harris: We have native integrations for Splunk, Datadog logs, and export to S3, and webhooks for syslog pickup. We'll attach a list of supported SIEM and examples.
[05:20] Julia Park: Great. A couple of concerns we've heard internally: model artifacts caching and KV cache — are there any encryption concerns for cached prompt data?
[05:30] Leo Harris: Caching respects encryption at rest for all persisted caches. For in-memory KV cache it's ephemeral and not persisted to disk unless configured; for sensitive workloads we disable persistent caching and use secure enclaves on Dedicated/Private.
[05:44] Maya Chen: Also want to call out routing and fallback - if we route to cheaper model variants is customer data ever sent to a different tenancy? Short answer: no, data stays within the customer's configured tenancy and region; we may route to compatible model variants but in Hosted those variants are controlled by Redwood with same data controls. We'll provide precise language.
[06:03] Marcus Lee: Sounds promising. Can we get a short pilot? We want to run a benchmark and some compliance tests.
[06:08] Maya Chen: Absolutely — we can provision a Dedicated trial cluster for benchmarking, or a Private eval if you prefer. For the pilot we'll need an IP allowlist, SAML metadata, and a list of test vectors.
[06:19] Julia Park: Legal will want the data processing addendum and terms. Anika will coordinate.
[06:23] Anika Patel: Yes, I'll circulate our standard questionnaire. We'll expect the SOC2 docs and sample DPA.
[06:29] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll attach SOC2/ISO, DPA template, SAML integration guide, RBAC examples, and infra diagrams.
[06:36] Julia Park: One more thing — how do you handle data deletion requests? If a user requests deletion, is model fine-tuning data swept?
[06:43] Leo Harris: We have documented deletion flows: for Hosted we remove records from active storage and purge caches per retention; with Dedicated/Private we can provide stronger guarantees and support deletion from datasets used in fine-tuning only if the model training pipelines include that dataset. We'll include the official deletion policy and timelines.
[07:01] Marcus Lee: Ok that's all I have.
[07:03] Maya Chen: Recap of next steps: we'll send artifacts (SOC2/ISO, DPA, SSO guide, infra diagrams), Leo will produce the VPC/KMS flow, and Arclight will share the compliance questionnaire and desired retention buckets. Follow-up call with infra+legal next Tuesday, propose 50-minute slot.
[07:18] Julia Park: That works. Thanks for the quick answers — this was helpful.
[07:22] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll email the packet by end of day tomorrow and set up the follow-up.
[07:28] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (SAML sometimes transcribed as "Sam L", KMS spelled "K-M-S"), filler words and brief crosstalk. The team prefers a follow-up with full SE infra deep dive and legal on the DPA/contracting path.
